maya: Heads-up — p99 jumped on dedicated-prod after the v8.2 rollout at ~12:04UTC. Not huge in error rate but latency spike steady for last 20m :eyes:
jen: seeing it on dashboards too. p50 unchanged, p99 -> +120ms on text-generation route. rolling logs now.
tariq: kernel-decider logs show a lot of churn — switching from optimized_avx to fallback_quant path mid-request. looks like kernel selector mispredicts when seq_len > 512.
liam: repro profile from a noisy host pinned to the same GPU pool shows KV cache hit rate collapse. attaching counters:
```
kv_cache.hits: 0.19
kv_cache.requests: 1.2k
avg_seq_len: 716
avg_batch_size: 5.1
kernel_switches/sec: 42
memcpy_bytes/sec: 1.8GB
```
maya: deploy-bot shows canary finished and then full rollout started at 12:01 — deploy-bot, can you paste rollout IDs?
deploy-bot: rollout:v8.2 -> traffic:100% (canary:v8.2-rc3 @12:01:19) :white_check_mark:
jen: interesting — v8.2 changed tokenizer to newer merge rules; that can increase subtoken count for some payloads. more subtokens => larger effective seq_len => different kernel path.
tariq: confirms. kernel selector is using a seqlen threshold heuristic + runtime mem pressure. When avg_seq_len crosses 512, it prefers fallback_quant which has worse p99 for long tails. the tokenizer change pushes many requests over threshold.
liam: also seeing KV cache key fragmentation — more prefixes means fewer cache hits. kv cache hit rate fell from ~0.78 -> 0.19 on affected tenants. That causes more KV loads + cache miss prefetch, increasing memcpy and contention.
jen: can we patch quicker? options: 1) rollback v8.2 full rollout, 2) change kernel decision thresholds to favor optimized_avx for short bursts, or 3) enable tokenizer-shim at runtime to map new subtokens back to old merge behavior for canary tenants.
sre-oncall: rollback is safest short-term. we're seeing user-facing latency. recommend immediate rollback and follow-up fix.
maya: agreed. rolling back now to v8.1. deploy-bot can you kick?
deploy-bot: rollback:start rollback:v8.1 -> target:dedicated-prod @12:22:11
jen: after rollback, we should run a controlled canary with instrumented kernel-decider + kv tracing to measure where fragmentation occurs. also add a temporary override: force_kernel=optimized_avx for the affected shard so we can confirm kernel impact without full rollback.
tariq: I'll draft a hotfix patch to adjust selector threshold and add a safety flag (env FORCE_KERNEL_LEGACY) so we can toggle quickly. won't change model behavior.
liam: follow-up: batcher heuristics need to group by encoded-length bucket rather than raw tokens. current hint uses token count which is inconsistent across tokenizers. will open PR to use encoded_bytes/approx_seq_len as hint.
maya: action items — jira: PERF-2213 rollback done, PERF-2214 run instrumented canary, PERF-2215 selector threshold hotfix, PERF-2216 batcher hint PR. assigning: rollback=maya, canary=jen, selector=tariq, batcher=liam.
jen: added an eval suite against recent production prompts to measure subtoken distribution; will post results in this thread when ready. :mag:
liam: question — any noisy-tenant signatures? I saw one tenant spike was co-located and had high concurrent streaming calls yesterday. could amplify kernel churn.
tariq: noted. will add noisy-tenant label to query for postmortem.
jen: quick sanity log snippet from kernel-decider at 12:10:
```
[12:10:03] req=0x7f3a kernel_decider chosen=fallback_quant reason=seq_len(682)>512 and mem_pressure(low)
[12:10:03] req=0x7f3a kv_cache.hit=false prefix_len=24
[12:10:03] req=0x7f3a batch_size=3 latency_ms=42
```
maya: good capture. once rollback completes, let's validate p99 back to baseline and then run canary with FORCE_KERNEL_LEGACY first, then tokenizer shim test.
jen: will run eval and report. thanks all. :thumbsup:
